To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the three-nucleon break-up reaction in a nuclear environment can be described by a simple extension of the free space reaction, which is based on a density-dependent modification of the two-nucleon break up cross section, and that the break-up of deuterons in nuclear matter is strongly enhanced by the nuclear environment.
the break-up cross section is enhanced by a factor of 3.5 at the saturation density of nuclear matter, and by a factor of two at the density of the inner core of heavy nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the three-nucleon problem in a nuclear environment.
the investigation of the medium modifications of the nucleonic properties, in particular the nucleon-nucleon ( NN ) interaction, in nuclear matter.
the investigation of nuclear reactions in the medium and the study of the nuclear equation of state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Faddeeva approach is a useful and reliable tool in the description of the three-nucleon problem.
the in-medium break up cross section is strongly enhanced by a factor of two at normal nuclear density.
the Faddeeva technique is a useful and powerful tool to study the medium modifications of nuclear reactions in a nuclear environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in-medium effects on the NNN scattering amplitude are mainly due to the Pauli blocking and to the medium polarization, and the latter is the dominant one.

the medium modifications of the nucleonic properties, such as the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, the nucleon effective mass and the nucleon-nuclear optical potential, are the main reasons of the medium modifications of three-nucleon reactions.
the in-medium break up cross section is enhanced by a factor of 1.5 at a nuclear density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the medium modification of the NNN scattering amplitude is dominated by the medium modification of two-nucleon scattering amplitudes.
, at finite density, the break-up reaction is strongly enhanced, and therefore it can be a very efficient channel for the formation of deuterons in a nuclear medium.
the break-up cross section of deuterons in the medium is a crucial ingredient in the description of the dynamics of the nuclear matter.
